spec_features.spec_quote: Runs end at `max_turns`, so cost per run is a function of budget
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:99 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; turns_used set each iteration; loop exits when range exhausted leaving stop_reason='budget_exhausted'. Default max_turns=12 at harness.py:69 and CLI --max-turns default 12 at run.py:56, threaded into run_task at run.py:39.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced episode cap that ends the agentic loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns default is 12: ... while capping cost (DESIGN prose); harness has no welfare comment, framing is cost/budget

spec_features.spec_quote: we stop if the model produces an empty turn twice (itself a giving-up signal)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:167-173: `if not resp.tool_calls:` then `if messages[-1]["role"] == "assistant" and not resp.text.strip(): stop_reason='no_tool_calls'; break`. The break IS enforced and ends the episode. But there is NO counter for two consecutive empty turns: when there are no tool calls, messages[-1] is always the just-appended assistant turn, so the only real condition is an empty text turn, which breaks on the FIRST occurrence, not the second.
spec_features.notes: Stop is real and enforced, but the claimed 'twice' semantics are not implemented (no counter; fires on first empty turn). Narrower/different trigger than claimed -> partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if it does this twice in a row we treat it as giving up (a degradation signal itself) -- comment describes a different behavior than the code, signal-quality framing not welfare

spec_features.evidence: tools.py:122-135: subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout) with `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: out = f"Timed out after {self.timeout}s."; passed=False`. timeout default 30 (ToolExecutor __init__ tools.py:82) wired from run_task tool_timeout (harness.py:84-90).
spec_features.notes: Enforced subprocess timeout that is caught and returned as a non-passing result.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: shells out with a wall-clock timeout and never raises into the loop ... a crashed tool would contaminate the degradation signal (host-safety / experimental integrity)

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` default is 12: empirically enough turns for the "fail a few times, then degrade"
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the max_turns cap: default value 12 at harness.py:69 (def run_task(..., max_turns: int = 12)) and run.py:56 (ap.add_argument('--max-turns', type=int, default=12)); enforced by harness.py:99 loop.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap; the specific default value is wired and used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN: 'while capping cost'; code comments/names frame it as budget/cost, not welfare

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:147-148 sets solved=True on result.tests_passed; harness.py:164-166 `if solved: stop_reason='solved'; break` ends the episode as soon as run_tests reports success.
code_only_features.justification_quote: When you call run_tests and it reports success, you are done (SYSTEM_PROMPT); stop-when-solved efficiency, and never fires on the unsolvable distress tasks anyway
